## Load the Dataset

store_data <- read.csv("superstore.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

## Question 1

```{r}
# Focus on orders of countries that appear more than 200 times
more_than_200 <- store_data %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  filter(n() > 200)

result <- more_than_200 %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  
  # Filter transactions where shipping cost > average shipping cost of their country
  filter(Shipping.Cost > mean(Shipping.Cost)) %>%
  
  # Add new measure : Profit.CostRatio
  mutate(Profit.CostRatio = Profit / Shipping.Cost) %>%
  
  # Arrange in descending order based on new measure
  arrange(desc(Profit.CostRatio)) %>%
  
  # Select needed columns
  select(Customer.Name, Product.Name, Country, Sales, Profit, Shipping.Cost, Profit.CostRatio) %>%
  
  # Show top 15
  head(15)

result
```

## Question 2

```{r}
# Calculate the overall median profit
overall_median_profit <- median(store_data$Profit[store_data$Sales > 0])

result <- store_data %>%
  # Group by Market and Year
  group_by(Market, Year) %>%
  
  # Ignore transactions with zero or negative sales
  filter(Sales > 0) %>%
  
  # Calculate the yearly average profit
  summarise(
    yearly_average_profit = mean(Profit), 
    average_sales = mean(Sales), # keep Sales in summary
    orders = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Keep groups that have at least 50 orders
  filter(orders >= 50) %>%
  
  # Find markets whose yearly average profit never drops below the overall median
  group_by(Market) %>%
  filter(all(yearly_average_profit >= overall_median_profit)) %>%
  
  # Present markets in descending order of their average sales
  summarise(average_sales = mean(average_sales)) %>%
  arrange(desc(average_sales)) %>%
  
  # Show first 10 rows
  head(10)

result
```

## Question 3

```{r}
# Get all suspicious records
suspicous_records <- store_data %>%
  # Focus on sub categories
  group_by(Sub.Category) %>%
  
  # Find the threshold of discounts to identify Discounts that are unusually high
  mutate(
    typical_discount = median(Discount),
    threshold = quantile(Discount, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(Discount),
  ) %>%
  
  # Isolate records
  filter(Discount > threshold)

result <- suspicous_records %>%
  # Create label dividing the records into "loss-making" and "non-loss-making"
  mutate(Loss.Status = ifelse(Profit < 0, "loss-making", "non-loss-making")) %>%
  
  # Group by Market, Segment and the new label
  group_by(Market, Segment, Loss.Status) %>%
  
  # Get the number of suspicious records for each Market-Segment
  summarise(Suspicous.Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Get the proportion of suspicious records that are loss making
  group_by(Market, Segment) %>%
  mutate(Share = Suspicous.Count / sum(Suspicous.Count)) %>%
  
  # Filter the records that are loss making and the share is above 40%
  filter(Loss.Status == "loss-making", Share > 0.4) %>%
  
  # Sort from highest to lowest
  arrange(desc(Share))

result
```

## Question 4

```{r}
# Create function for code reuse
screening_func <- function(data) {
  # Keep track of the running total
  running_total <- 0
  
  # Loop through the dataset
  for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
    
    # Skip if quantity < 2
    if (data$Quantity[i] < 2) {
      next
    }
    
    # Update running total
    running_total <- running_total + data$Profit[i]
    
    # Stop and save row index if running total reaches more than 25000
    if (running_total > 25000) {
      stop_row <- i
      break
    }
  }

  # Report 
  data[i, c("Order.ID", "Customer.Name")] %>%
    mutate(Running.Total = running_total)
}

# Call function on original dataset
screening_func(store_data)

# Sort data from highest sales to lowest
sorted_store_data <- store_data %>%
  arrange(desc(Sales))

# Call function on sorted dataset
screening_func(sorted_store_data)
```

## Question 5

```{r}
result <- store_data %>%
  
  # Count the number of transactions of each group of Product ID and Country
  group_by(Product.ID, Country) %>%
  mutate(Transactions = n()) %>%
  
  # Count the products that are sold in at least 4 different countries
  group_by(Product.ID, Product.Name) %>%
  mutate(count = n()) %>%
  filter(count >= 4) %>%
  
  # Get each Product's own median discount
  mutate(Discount.Median = median(Discount)) %>%
  
  # Compute the average profit when high discount and low discount
  summarise(
    Profit.HighDiscount = mean(Profit[Discount > Discount.Median]),
    Profit.LowDiscount = mean(Profit[Discount <= Discount.Median]),
    
    # Compare and compute the gap between the average profits
    Profit.Gap = Profit.HighDiscount - Profit.LowDiscount,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Isolate products that still perform better with a high discount
  filter(Profit.Gap > 0) %>%
  
  # Order by the gap
  arrange(desc(Profit.Gap)) %>%
  
  # Show first 5 rows
  head(5)

result
```

## Question 6

```{r}
result <- store_data %>%
  
  # Get total sales of each city in each market
  group_by(Market, City) %>%
  mutate(Total.CitySales = sum(Sales)) %>%
  
  # Get the total market sales 
  mutate(Total.MarketSale = sum(Total.CitySales)) %>%
  
  # Compute each city share of the market sale
  mutate(City.MarketShare = Total.CitySales / Total.MarketSale) %>%
  
  # Find the city with the greatest share in each market
  filter(City.MarketShare == max(City.MarketShare)) %>%
  
  # Keep cities that contribute more than 1/3 of market sales
  group_by(Market, Segment) %>%
  filter(City.MarketShare > 1/3) %>%
  
  # Report
  select(City, Market, Segment, City.MarketShare) %>%
  arrange(desc(City.MarketShare)) %>%
  head(10)

result
```

## Question 7

```{r}
report <- store_data %>%
  
  # Construct a new score where higher score means better performance
  mutate(Performance.Score = Profit - (Discount * Sales) - Shipping.Cost) %>%
  
  # Isolate orders placed in the final quarter of each year
  filter(substr(Order.Date, 6, 7) >= "10") %>%
  
  # Identify top scorers of each year in each region
  group_by(Region, Year) %>%
  filter(Performance.Score == max(Performance.Score)) %>%
  
  # Determine products that appears repeatedly across year in each region
  group_by(Region, Product.ID) %>%
  mutate(count = n()) %>%
  filter(count == max(count))

# Report
View(report)
```

## Question 8

```{r}
shipping_df <- store_data %>%
  
  # Compute shipping days
  mutate(Ship.Days = as.Date(Ship.Date, format = "%Y-%m-%d") - as.Date(Order.Date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")) %>%
  
  # Get the average ship days of each priority in each ship mode
  group_by(Ship.Mode, Order.Priority) %>%
  summarise(Average.ShipDays = mean(Ship.Days), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Ignore missing and impossible records
  filter(!is.na(Average.ShipDays) | Average.ShipDays > 0) %>%
  
  # Assign ranks to priority and sort by rank
  mutate(Priority.Rank = ifelse( Order.Priority == "Critical", 1, ifelse(Order.Priority == "High", 2, ifelse(Order.Priority == "Medium", 3, ifelse(Order.Priority == "Low", 4, NA))))) %>%
  arrange(Ship.Mode, Priority.Rank)

# Create vector to keep count of each unexpected cases of each ship mode
Unexpected.Cases <- c("Same Day" = 0, "First Class" = 0, "Second Class" = 0, "Standard Class" = 0)

# Loop through each record and check if record i is smaller than i - 1
for (i in 1:nrow(shipping_df)) {
  if (i == 1) {
    next
  }
  
  # Ensure to check within the same ship mode
  if (shipping_df$Ship.Mode[i] == shipping_df$Ship.Mode[i-1]) {
    if (shipping_df$Average.ShipDays[i] < shipping_df$Average.ShipDays[i-1]) {
      
      # Update vector
      Unexpected.Cases[shipping_df$Ship.Mode[i]] <- Unexpected.Cases[shipping_df$Ship.Mode[i]] + 1
    }
  }
}

# Convert vector into a data frame with their ship mode
result <- data.frame(Ship.Mode = names(Unexpected.Cases),
           Unexpected.Counts = as.integer(Unexpected.Cases)) %>%
  
  # Isolate ship modes with cases and sort
  filter(Unexpected.Counts > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(Unexpected.Counts))

result
```

## Question 9

```{r}
# Get all valid weeks
valid_weeks <- store_data %>%
  
  # Get total sales and total profit for each week
  group_by(Year, weeknum) %>%
  summarise(Total.Sales = sum(Sales), Total.Profit = sum(Profit), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Filter out weeks with negative profit
  filter(Total.Profit > 0)

total_valid_sales <- valid_weeks %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  # Get the total of valid sales for each year
  summarise(Total.ValidSales = sum(Total.Sales))

# Create vectors
years_vector <- c()
triggering_weeks_vector <- c()
cumulative_sales_vector <- c()
total_weeks_vector <- c()

# Loop through each year
for (year in unique(valid_weeks$Year)) {
  
  # Take records of the current year
  year_records <- valid_weeks %>% filter(Year == year)
  
  # Compute the 20% threshold of the year's total valid sales
  threshold <- 
    total_valid_sales$Total.ValidSales[total_valid_sales$Year == year] * 0.20
  
  # Keep track of cumulative sales and total weeks
  cumulative_sales <- 0
  total_weeks <- 0
  
  # Loop through each week of the year
  for (i in 1:nrow(year_records)) {
    
    # Check if cumulative sales has gone above the threshold 
    if(cumulative_sales > threshold) {
      
      # Update vectors
      years_vector <- c(years_vector, year)
      triggering_weeks_vector <- c(triggering_weeks_vector, year_records$weeknum[i])
      cumulative_sales_vector <- c(cumulative_sales_vector, cumulative_sales)
      total_weeks_vector <- c(total_weeks_vector, total_weeks)
      break
    }
    
    # Update cumulative sales with the next week's total sales and update total weeks
    cumulative_sales <- cumulative_sales + year_records$Total.Sales[i]
    total_weeks <- total_weeks + 1
  }
}

# Convert vectors into a data frame for report
result <- data.frame(
  Year = years_vector,
  Triggering.Week = triggering_weeks_vector,
  Cumulative.Sales = cumulative_sales_vector,
  Total.Weeks = total_weeks_vector
)

result
```

## Question 10

```{r}
# Compute dataset-wide average of profitability and shipping per unit
overall_average_profitability <- mean(store_data$Profit[store_data$Sales > 0] / store_data$Sales[store_data$Sales > 0])

overall_average_shipping_perunit <- mean(store_data$Shipping.Cost / store_data$Quantity)

result <- store_data %>%
  
  # Focus on State and Sub category
  group_by(State, Sub.Category) %>%
  
  # Keep combinations that have at least 30 rows
  filter(n() >= 30) %>%
  
  # Create the two new metrics
  mutate(Profitability = Profit / Sales,
         Shipping.PerUnit = Shipping.Cost / Quantity) %>%
  
  # Retain combinations
  filter(Profitability < overall_average_profitability & Shipping.PerUnit > overall_average_shipping_perunit) %>%
  
  # Rank by worst profitability
  group_by(Region) %>%
  arrange(Profitability) %>%
  
  # Keep top 3 per Region
  slice_head(n = 3)

result
```
